summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy with ejection fraction of 10%, end-stage renal disease on dialysis, and cryptogenic organizing pneumonia, was readmitted two days after discharge for recurrent syncope and worsening shortness of breath. He was found to have large bilateral pleural effusions and severe heart failure with a BNP over 70,000. He developed hypotension during dialysis and was transitioned to CRRT, which he could not tolerate. His respiratory status deteriorated, requiring bilateral chest tube placement for pleural fluid drainage. Despite interventions, his condition declined due to acute on chronic heart and respiratory failure. After discussions with family, care was transitioned to comfort measures only, and he passed away peacefully with family at the bedside.
problems: Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure and with stage 5 chronic kidney disease, or end stage renal disease
Rheumatic disorders of both mitral and tricuspid valves
Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Personal history of other malignant neoplasm of skin
Adverse effect of antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs, sequela
